Which risk factors are too heterogeneous.vetted_answer: The maternal risk factors with the strongest, most consistent effect on pregnancy-associated VTE are previous_VTE (RR 24.834, 95% CI 21.278 to 28.984, 6 studies), thrombophilia (RR 9.417, 95% CI 7.575 to 11.706, 5 studies), obesity_bmi_over_30 (RR 2.398, 95% CI 1.996 to 2.881, 7 studies), emergency_caesarean (RR 2.107, 95% CI 1.808 to 2.454, 5 studies), multiple_pregnancy (RR 1.993, 95% CI 1.575 to 2.524, 5 studies), age_over_35 (RR 1.58, 95% CI 1.298 to 1.922, 6 studies). Ranked individually, previous_VTE and thrombophilia contribute most. The panel does not report a single combined absolute risk here: multiplying pooled ratios of this size implies about 672.96 per 1000, which is not credible. A joint absolute risk should come from a model fitted on individuals who carry these factors together, not from multiplying marginal pooled ratios. The panel does not report a single pooled estimate for immobility: its effect varies too much across populations (I²=86.2%) to trust as one number. Pooling here would hide the disagreement, not resolve it.
